Triggers.value: Visible injuries or wounds on others
Physical pain in a part of the body

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I frequently look behind me to check if someone is following me
I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
There is something about me that made the event happen

vignette: Carlos, a 53-year-old Latin American man, has been seeking help for symptoms that have increasingly plagued his daily life. His experience with police violence during an altercation at a community meeting six months ago triggered a cascade of traumatic memories and fears. At the time, Carlos had attended the meeting to advocate for better neighborhood safety measures but was mistakenly identified as a troublemaker by the police officers on duty. The ensuing confrontation left him with visible injuries and deep emotional scars. Since that night, Carlos has been hyper-vigilant about his surroundings, always scanning his environment for potential threats. His fear of unfamiliar places is particularly pronounced; he avoids going to new locations because he feels unable to assess the danger accurately. This avoidance has affected his work as a tax consultant significantly. He now rarely attends networking events or client meetings outside of his familiar office space. When he does venture out, he compulsively looks behind him and meticulously plans escape routes in case of another encounter with authorities. The traumatic event left Carlos with visible injuries that still remind him of the violence he endured. Even minor physical pain can trigger intense flashbacks and anxiety. One day at work, a sudden twinge in his arm sent him spiraling back to the night of the altercation. He became acutely aware of every detail-the cold metal cuffs on his wrists, the harsh words from the officers, and the fear he felt as he was taken away. These memories are particularly potent because they remind Carlos not just of the event itself but also of the helplessness he experienced. Carlos's negative appraisals have further exacerbated his symptoms. He feels deeply isolated and set apart from others, believing that there is something inherently wrong with him that made the event happen. This belief has led to significant withdrawal from social interactions. His divorce only a year ago has compounded these feelings of isolation. Despite attempts to reconnect with friends and family, Carlos often finds himself pushing them away, convinced that he cannot trust anyone. His negative thoughts have also affected his sense of purpose. He is no longer certain if his life is worth living, which has led him to consider drastic measures. The weight of this belief has made it difficult for him to engage in activities he once enjoyed, such as attending cultural events or visiting family gatherings. What finally brought Carlos to seek help was a particularly disturbing episode at work. During a routine meeting with clients, the sound of police sirens outside triggered a panic attack. He felt trapped and unable to escape, despite being in his familiar office environment. The sheer intensity of his reaction made him realize that he needed professional support to navigate these overwhelming emotions. In therapy, Carlos hopes to regain a sense of control over his life and reduce the debilitating fear that has been holding him back. What frightens him most is the possibility that he might never feel safe again. He is also hopeful that with support, he can rebuild connections with others and find meaning in his daily activities once more. Through this process, Carlos aims to understand why certain triggers are so potent for him and learn strategies to manage his anxiety without resorting to avoidance behaviors. His journey toward healing begins with acknowledging the profound impact of the traumatic event and finding ways to integrate these experiences into a more balanced and fulfilling life.
